maria: FYI ran a quick perf sweep after swapping the default kernel for r/stream routes. p95 jumped on a couple of tiers.
chen: ugh. which kernel swap? the avx-fused one? :grimace:
maria: yes, avx-fused + new GEMM schedule. looked fine in microbenchmarks but system p95 for route=chat/stream tier=free went 185ms -> 312ms.
alex: interesting. did kv-hit rate change? could be cache alignment/regressions on prefix sharing.
maria: KV hit ratio stayed ~82% for long-tail requests, but median tokens per request increased a bit (from 42 -> 58) due to a client change. still doesn't fully explain the p95 jump.
nora: can you paste the trace? especially batch sizes and microbatch allocation around the spike.
maria: pasted flame and a short log snippet:
```
# timestamp 2026-03-15T09:41:02Z
route=chat/stream tier=free batch_size=16 avg_microbatch=4 kv_hit=0.82 kernel=avx-fused p95=312ms
batcher: token_budget_target=64 route_budget=default queue_weight=1.0
```
sam: the token_budget_target=64 for free tier is aggressive. with median tokens rising we may be letting too many requests into microbatches and causing kernel contention.
chen: agree. we should try SLO-driven budget: scale token_budget_target per-route with p95 feedback.
perfbot: perf-alert: p95_increase_detected route=chat/stream previous_p95=185ms current_p95=312ms delta=+68%
infra-bot: deploy started: batcher/prefetcher rollback candidate v3 -> v2
alex: before a rollback, can we try tuning queue_weight and dynamic token cap? small sweep: reduce route_budget by 25% and lower token_budget_target to 48.
maria: ran an A/B (10k reqs) with token_budget_target=48 and queue_weight=0.8. p95 dropped to 198ms on the A group.
chen: that's promising. do we see any increase in cold-starts or KV miss amplification? maria?
maria: KV miss rate unchanged, but CPU scheduler shows fewer preemptions when microbatch size stayed <8.
nora: can we automate this as a feedback controller? idea: maintain target_p95 per route (e.g., 200ms free, 120ms pro) and adjust token_budget_target by -10%/+5% per evaluation window.
sam: pseudocode:
```
if observed_p95 > target_p95: token_budget *= 0.9
else if observed_p95 < target_p95*0.85: token_budget *= 1.05
clamp token_budget between min,max per tier
```

alex: need safety: don't change token budget by >30% per hour and add cooldown for kernel handoffs.
chen: also factor in kernel affinity: some kernels handle wider microbatches better. Controller should be aware of current kernel and compute capacity.
perfbot: note: kernel-switch events correlate with 2x variance in throughput for long sequences.
maria: action items from this thread:
- roll batcher back? currently rolled to v2 candidate for affected cluster (infra-bot)
- implement feedback controller (nora + sam) for route/tier token budgets
- add kernel-aware weighting to controller (chen + alex)
- better perf regression test that runs realistic interleaving sequences + kv-access pattern (maria)

nora: I'll open a small RFC and a lightweight controller PoC: we can tune windows to 30s and use exponential moving average for p95.
sam: I'll add an e2e canary that injects longer sequences and measures effect on p95 and kv churn.
chen: also want a probe that forces kernel-select by setting a synthetic sequence length and measuring microbatch occupation.
alex: pinging @ops for capacity scheduling notes — might need to throttle free-tier routes during kernel transitions.
ops: saw the perf-alert, thumbs-up to the controller approach. prefer gradual ramp rather than sudden caps.
maria: thanks all. I'll keep the canary running and post graphs to the perf dashboard: https://dashboards.redwood.internal/perf/6323456789
chen: cool. if A/B stays stable for 12h, let's promote token_budget_target=48 for free tier and queue_weight=0.85 for chat/stream.
perfbot: resolved_checklist: controller_prototype=todo kernel_awareness=todo rollback_status=deployed_to_candidate
maria: closing out — will update thread when RFC is live. :thumbsup:
